The name also belongs to Joshua the high priest in the post-exilic community (Hag 1:1; Zech 3:1). The later contracted form Yeshua became the Hebrew name behind the Greek Iesous -- Jesus -- making this name a bridge between the Old and New Testaments. Spanish 'Josue,' French 'Josue,' and German 'Josua' all preserve the connection."
